title: 👑 Elite Challenge ⭐⭐⭐⭐: Master of the Four Seasons

questions.prompt: Three of these sentences about the weather are correct. Which one is NOT correct?
questions.explanation: The faulty sentence is the one with snows: after will the verb stays bare, so it must be It will snow tomorrow. The three others are right because will and won't keep their verb bare, and because It's is correctly followed by an adjective.

questions.prompt: In which pair are both words correctly spelled?

options.text: sun becomes sunny, hot becomes hotter
rain becomes rainny, cold becomes colder
wind becomes winddy, warm becomes warmmer
snow becomes snowwy, cool becomes cooller

questions.explanation: Sun and hot are both consonant plus vowel plus consonant, so both double their last letter: sunny and hotter. The other pairs double a letter that must stay single: rain and cool have two vowels before their last letter, snow ends in a w, and wind and warm end in two consonants. The right forms there are rainy, snowy, windy, warmer and cooler.

questions.prompt: Read: "In Tunisia April is warmer than February, and July is warmer than April." Which sentence is true?
questions.explanation: Follow the two comparisons in one line: February, then April above it, then July above April. July is therefore the warmest of the three and February the coldest, so July is warmer than February. Each of the other sentences turns one of the two given comparisons upside down.

questions.prompt: Read: "Next Sunday there will be no cloud and the sun will be strong." Which sentence about next Sunday is correct?
questions.explanation: A sky with no cloud and a strong sun makes a sunny day, and the future needs will followed by the bare verb be: It will be sunny. Saying It will sunny loses the verb, It will be sun keeps the noun instead of the adjective, and It wills be sunny puts an -s on will.

questions.prompt: Which sentence about a winter activity is completely correct?

options.text: I enjoy walk in the fresh air with my boots.
I enjoy walking in the fresh air with my boots.
I enjoy to walk in the fresh air with my boots.
I enjoy walkking in the fresh air with my boots.

questions.explanation: After enjoy the activity takes the -ing form, so it is walking. The bare verb and the form with to never follow enjoy, and the spelling with two k doubles a letter that has an l in front of it, where nothing is doubled.

questions.prompt: In one of these four words the throat does NOT shake on the th. Which word is it?
questions.explanation: In teeth the th lets the air pass and the throat stays quiet. In weather, in mother and in this the throat shakes: those three carry the sound of the word the, and the spelling th is the same in all four, so only the ear can sort them.
